title: a corrupt page header sends sqlite3Get4byte past the end of the page buffer
upstream_fix: fz02 (R2 fuzz-corpus diff image; trigger re-derived by capstone 2026-10-03)
object: a page buffer of the page cache (pcache1)
lifetime_ender: not a lifetime defect: the read leaves the page buffer
reached_why: the image opened; s0_rc=11 (SQLITE_CORRUPT) on the dbstat statement means the engine rejected the image before the defect

layer_by_arm.default: pcache1 bulk pool (SQLITE_DEFAULT_PCACHE_INITSZ=20 pages carved from one block)

asan.why: the over-read stays inside the arena or the bulk pool; with INITSZ=0 every page is its own block with redzones; default arm measured 2026-11-16: the over-read leaves the pcache bulk block, so the default arm is reported, against a heap redzone or another block, never against the page

valgrind.why: same; default arm measured 2026-11-16: the over-read leaves the pcache bulk block, so the default arm is reported, against a heap redzone or another block, never against the page

lowfat.why: bounds come from the malloc'd block; the pool is one block

2026-11-16 lab server x86-64, formal (re.notes: memsys5: both tools silent, exit 0; the over-read stays in memory they consider valid. Default: both report, but not against the page: ASan finds the read in heap redzone memory (wild pointer), Memcheck 296 bytes inside a freed 1,016-byte block; the read leaves the pcache bulk block. Rewrite: ASan reports 253 bytes after a 784-byte page block. The macOS development run had ASan detect the memsys5 arm 1.9 KB past the arena: whether this stride leaves the arena depends on the layout.
